questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Golden Temple' (Harmandir Sahib) is located in which city?
questions.explanation: The Golden Temple (Sri Harmandir Sahib), the holiest Sikh shrine, is located in Amritsar, Punjab. Delhi is wrong — it has Gurudwara Bangla Sahib but not the Golden Temple. Jaipur is wrong — it is known for Hawa Mahal and Amber Fort. Varanasi is wrong — it is known for Kashi Vishwanath Temple.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about Indian languages:

(i) Hindi is the most widely spoken language in India.
(ii) The Eighth Schedule of the Constitution recognizes 22 scheduled languages.
(iii) English is listed as a scheduled language in India.
(iv) Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, and Malayalam are Dravidian languages.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Hindi (including its dialects) is India's most widely spoken language. (ii) is correct — the Eighth Schedule lists 22 languages (after Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, and Santhali were added in 2003). (iv) is correct — Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, and Malayalam belong to the Dravidian language family. (iii) is wrong — English is NOT a scheduled language; it has the status of 'subsidiary official language' but is not in the Eighth Schedule.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Taj Mahal, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is situated on the banks of which river?
questions.explanation: The Taj Mahal in Agra stands on the southern bank of the river Yamuna. Ganges is wrong — the Ganges flows through Varanasi and Allahabad, not Agra. Chambal is wrong — it flows through Rajasthan/MP. Godavari is wrong — it flows through Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Jaipur is called the 'Pink City'.
Reason (R): The old city buildings of Jaipur were painted terracotta pink in 1876 to welcome the Prince of Wales, and the tradition continues.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — Jaipur is famous as the Pink City. Reason (R) is also correct — Maharaja Ram Singh had the city painted pink for the royal visit. (R) explains (A) because the historical painting of buildings in pink is the reason for the name. Option 2 is wrong because (R) directly explains (A). Option 3 is wrong because (R) is historically accurate. Option 4 is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following cities with their popular names:

Column I:
(a) Varanasi
(b) Mumbai
(c) Hyderabad
(d) Kolkata

Column II:
(i) City of Joy
(ii) City of Pearls
(iii) Gateway of India
(iv) City of Temples / Spiritual Capital

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a) Varanasi = Spiritual Capital / City of Temples — matches (iv). (b) Mumbai = Gateway of India (also financial capital) — matches (iii). (c) Hyderabad = City of Pearls (pearl trade) — matches (ii). (d) Kolkata = City of Joy — matches (i). Option 2 swaps (a) and (b). Option 3 swaps (b) and (c). Option 4 swaps (c) and (d).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are classical languages of India recognized by the Government?

(i) Tamil
(ii) Sanskrit
(iii) English
(iv) Kannada

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) Tamil — granted classical language status in 2004 ✓. (ii) Sanskrit — granted classical status in 2005 ✓. (iv) Kannada — granted classical status in 2008 ✓. (iii) English is wrong — English has no classical language status in India; it is not an Indian-origin language.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The famous 'Valley of Flowers' National Park is located in which state?
questions.explanation: The Valley of Flowers, a UNESCO World Heritage Site known for its alpine flowers, is in the Chamoli district of Uttarakhand. Himachal Pradesh is wrong — it has its own flower valleys but not this UNESCO site. J&K is wrong — though it has beautiful valleys, this specific park is in Uttarakhand. Sikkim is wrong — located in the northeast.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about Indian states and their official languages:

(i) Maharashtra — Marathi
(ii) West Bengal — Bengali
(iii) Tamil Nadu — Hindi
(iv) Gujarat — Gujarati

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Marathi is Maharashtra's official language. (ii) is correct — Bengali is West Bengal's official language. (iv) is correct — Gujarati is Gujarat's official language. (iii) is wrong — Tamil Nadu's official language is TAMIL, not Hindi. Tamil Nadu has historically resisted Hindi imposition.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The famous Konark Sun Temple is located in the state of __________.
questions.explanation: The Konark Sun Temple (13th century, UNESCO World Heritage Site) is in Konark, Puri district, Odisha. Rajasthan is wrong — it has Dilwara Temples and forts. Madhya Pradesh is wrong — it has Khajuraho. Karnataka is wrong — it has Hampi.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): India is called a multilingual country.
Reason (R): India has 22 scheduled languages and hundreds of other languages and dialects spoken across its diverse regions.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — India is one of the world's most linguistically diverse countries. Reason (R) is also correct — with 22 scheduled languages and 19,500+ dialects. (R) explains (A) because this vast linguistic diversity is exactly what makes India multilingual. Option 2 is wrong because (R) directly explains (A). Option 3 is wrong because (R) is accurate. Option 4 is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Gateway of India' monument is located in:
questions.explanation: The Gateway of India (built 1924) is an arch-monument on the waterfront of Mumbai, overlooking the Arabian Sea. Delhi is wrong — it has India Gate (different). Chennai is wrong — it has Marina Beach. Kolkata is wrong — it has Victoria Memorial.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following states with their predominant languages:

Column I:
(a) Kerala
(b) Andhra Pradesh
(c) Punjab
(d) Assam

Column II:
(i) Assamese
(ii) Punjabi
(iii) Telugu
(iv) Malayalam

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a) Kerala — Malayalam — matches (iv). (b) Andhra Pradesh — Telugu — matches (iii). (c) Punjab — Punjabi — matches (ii). (d) Assam — Assamese — matches (i). Option 2 swaps (a) and (b). Option 3 swaps (b) and (c). Option 4 swaps (c) and (d).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which city is known as the 'Silicon Valley of India'?
questions.explanation: Bengaluru (Bangalore) is called the Silicon Valley of India due to its concentration of IT companies and tech startups. Hyderabad is wrong — it's called 'Cyberabad' but not Silicon Valley. Pune is wrong — it's an IT hub but doesn't hold this specific title. Chennai is wrong — it's known as the 'Detroit of India' (automobiles).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about UNESCO World Heritage Sites in India:

(i) The Taj Mahal is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
(ii) The Qutub Minar is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
(iii) India has no natural World Heritage Sites.
(iv) Hampi (Karnataka) is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Taj Mahal was designated in 1983. (ii) is correct — Qutub Minar complex was designated in 1993. (iv) is correct — Group of Monuments at Hampi was designated in 1986. (iii) is wrong — India has several NATURAL World Heritage Sites including Kaziranga, Manas, Sundarbans, Western Ghats, etc.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Char Minar' is a famous landmark of which city?
questions.explanation: The Charminar (Four Minarets), built in 1591 by Sultan Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah, is the iconic monument of Hyderabad. Lucknow is wrong — it is known for Bara Imambara. Agra is wrong — it is known for the Taj Mahal. Bhopal is wrong — it is known for Sanchi Stupa nearby.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Hindi is written in the Devanagari script.
Reason (R): The Indian Constitution (Article 343) specifies that the official language of the Union shall be Hindi in Devanagari script.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — Hindi uses Devanagari script. Reason (R) is also correct — Article 343(1) explicitly states this. (R) explains (A) as the constitutional basis for the script. Option 2 is wrong because (R) provides constitutional authority for (A). Option 3 is wrong because (R) is accurate. Option 4 is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following pairs (monument — city) are correctly matched?

(i) Victoria Memorial — Kolkata
(ii) Hawa Mahal — Jaipur
(iii) India Gate — Mumbai
(iv) Meenakshi Temple — Madurai

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) Victoria Memorial — Kolkata ✓. (ii) Hawa Mahal (Palace of Winds) — Jaipur ✓. (iv) Meenakshi Amman Temple — Madurai (Tamil Nadu) ✓. (iii) is wrong — India Gate is in NEW DELHI, not Mumbai. Mumbai has the Gateway of India (different monument).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The official language of the state of Goa is:
questions.explanation: Konkani is the official language of Goa (recognised in the Eighth Schedule). Marathi is wrong — though widely spoken in Goa, Konkani is the official language. Portuguese is wrong — it was used during colonial rule but is no longer official. Hindi is wrong — it's not Goa's state language.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following famous places with the states they are in:

Column I:
(a) Ajanta & Ellora Caves
(b) Khajuraho Temples
(c) Sun Temple (Konark)
(d) Mysore Palace

Column II:
(i) Karnataka
(ii) Odisha
(iii) Maharashtra
(iv) Madhya Pradesh

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a) Ajanta & Ellora — Maharashtra (Aurangabad) — matches (iii). (b) Khajuraho — Madhya Pradesh (Chhatarpur) — matches (iv). (c) Sun Temple Konark — Odisha (Puri) — matches (ii). (d) Mysore Palace — Karnataka — matches (i). Option 2 swaps (a) and (b). Option 3 swaps (b) and (c). Option 4 swaps (c) and (d).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Udaipur, known as the 'City of Lakes', is located in which state?
questions.explanation: Udaipur (City of Lakes) is in southern Rajasthan, famous for Lake Pichola, Fateh Sagar, and the City Palace. Madhya Pradesh is wrong — it has Bhopal (City of Lakes but different). Gujarat is wrong — neighboring state. Maharashtra is wrong — far to the south.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Eighth Schedule languages:

(i) Dogri was added to the Eighth Schedule in 2003.
(ii) Sindhi is one of the 22 scheduled languages.
(iii) All scheduled languages have their own separate states.
(iv) Maithili was added to the Eighth Schedule in 2003.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Dogri (spoken mainly in Jammu) was added in 2003 by the 92nd Amendment. (ii) is correct — Sindhi is one of the 22 scheduled languages. (iv) is correct — Maithili (spoken in Bihar) was added in 2003. (iii) is wrong — not all scheduled languages have separate states (e.g., Sindhi, Sanskrit, Maithili, Bodo don't have their own states).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Sanchi Stupa, a famous Buddhist monument, is located in:
questions.explanation: The Great Stupa at Sanchi (built by Emperor Ashoka, 3rd century BC) is in Raisen district, Madhya Pradesh. Uttar Pradesh is wrong — it has Sarnath. Bihar is wrong — it has Bodh Gaya. Maharashtra is wrong — it has Ajanta/Ellora.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The language with the largest number of speakers in India after Hindi is __________.
questions.explanation: Bengali is the second most spoken language in India (after Hindi) with approximately 97 million speakers (2011 Census). Telugu is wrong — it is third. Marathi is wrong — it ranks fourth. Tamil is wrong — it has fewer speakers than Bengali.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following cities are correctly nicknamed?

(i) Chennai — Detroit of India (automobile industry)
(ii) Ahmedabad — Manchester of India (textile industry)
(iii) Jamshedpur — Steel City of India
(iv) Varanasi — Garden City of India

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) Chennai = Detroit of India (major auto hub: Hyundai, Ford, BMW) ✓. (ii) Ahmedabad = Manchester of India (textile mills) ✓. (iii) Jamshedpur = Steel City (Tata Steel headquarters) ✓. (iv) is wrong — Bengaluru is the 'Garden City of India', NOT Varanasi. Varanasi is the 'Spiritual Capital'.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Agra is one of the most visited tourist destinations in India.
Reason (R): Agra is home to three UNESCO World Heritage Sites — the Taj Mahal, Agra Fort, and Fatehpur Sikri.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — Agra attracts millions of domestic and international tourists annually. Reason (R) is also correct — Taj Mahal, Agra Fort, and Fatehpur Sikri are all UNESCO sites near Agra. (R) explains (A) because these world-class monuments are exactly what draws tourists. Option 2 is wrong because (R) directly explains (A). Option 3 is wrong because (R) is accurate. Option 4 is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Golden Quadrilateral' highway project connects which four metro cities?
questions.explanation: The Golden Quadrilateral connects India's four major metro cities — Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, and Kolkata — forming a quadrilateral of approximately 5,846 km. The other options list incorrect city combinations.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following scripts with their languages:

Column I:
(a) Devanagari
(b) Gurmukhi
(c) Bengali/Eastern Nagari
(d) Kannada script

Column II:
(i) Kannada
(ii) Hindi, Marathi, Sanskrit
(iii) Punjabi
(iv) Bengali, Assamese

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a) Devanagari is used for Hindi, Marathi, Sanskrit — matches (ii). (b) Gurmukhi is used for Punjabi — matches (iii). (c) Bengali/Eastern Nagari script is used for Bengali and Assamese — matches (iv). (d) Kannada script is used for Kannada — matches (i). Option 2 swaps (a) and (b). Option 3 swaps (b) and (c). Option 4 swaps (c) and (d).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements:

(i) Hampi is located in Karnataka and was the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire.
(ii) Fatehpur Sikri was built by Akbar near Agra.
(iii) The Red Fort in Delhi was built by Shah Jahan.
(iv) The Qutub Minar was built by Mahatma Gandhi.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Hampi in Karnataka was the Vijayanagara Empire's capital (14th–16th century). (ii) is correct — Fatehpur Sikri was built by Mughal Emperor Akbar in 1571 near Agra. (iii) is correct — Red Fort (Lal Qila) in Delhi was built by Shah Jahan in 1639. (iv) is wrong — Qutub Minar was built by Qutb-ud-din Aibak (c. 1193), NOT Mahatma Gandhi.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Sundarbans', the world's largest mangrove forest, is located in:
questions.explanation: The Sundarbans, a UNESCO World Heritage Site and home to the Royal Bengal Tiger, spans the delta of the Ganges in West Bengal (India) and Bangladesh. Kerala is wrong — it has backwaters but not Sundarbans. Odisha is wrong — it has Bhitarkanika mangroves but not Sundarbans. Gujarat is wrong — it has the Gir Forest.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are correctly paired (language family — languages)?

(i) Indo-Aryan — Hindi, Bengali, Gujarati
(ii) Dravidian — Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam
(iii) Sino-Tibetan — Manipuri, Bodo
(iv) Austric — English, French

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Hindi, Bengali, Gujarati are Indo-Aryan languages (largest family in India). (ii) is correct — Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam are Dravidian languages. (iii) is correct — Manipuri (Meitei) and Bodo belong to the Sino-Tibetan/Tibeto-Burman family. (iv) is wrong — English and French are Indo-European languages from EUROPE, not part of India's Austric family. Indian Austric languages include Santali and Mundari.
